newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks post modest morning advance.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks post modest morning advance.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks leaped sharply higher at the open on Tuesday morning on the back of Wall Street's second consecutive record high, before slipping back to show only modest gains, brokers said.
"Market sentiment is good," said Ronald Lam, chief dealer at Dao Heng Securities.
The Hang Seng Index advanced 70 points at the open before slipping back to show a 23-point rise to 11,590.88 on healthy turnover of HK$1.27 billion.
Brokers were very positive on the outlook for the Hong Kong market, despite its rapid gains of the past week.
"I am more positive now because the underlying fundamentals have changed," said David Williamson, sales director at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.

Williamson said the record high in the Dow Jones Industrial Average came following a dip in the U.S. long-bond yield below seven percent, suggesting that U.S. financial markets are betting the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates in its Federal Open Market Committee meeting on September 24.
The hefty increased in traded volume is also a bullish sign, brokers said.
"I also do not believe that funds are overweighted in this market. I think Asian strategists are likely to increase their weightings in Hong Kong in the fourth quarter," Williamson said.
The finance and property shares which have been the market's strongest leaders, underwent a mild bout of profit-taking in early Tuesday trading.

HSBC Holdings, however, bucked the trend and held steady, unchanged at HK$140.50, after briefly touching a new intra-day high of HK$142.00 in active trade. The bank's 61 percent held subsidiary Hang Seng Bank dipped HK$0.75 to HK81.00.
Both stocks are trading at or near their all time highs.
Henderson Land, which has risen sharply in the past two weeks, skipped to a new intra-day high of HK$65.75, before falling back to trade unchanged at HK$65.00.

Glorious Sun, which debuted at HK$2.20 compared with an offer price of HK$1.60, was the most active stock in terms of volume. The share rose to HK$2.45 before easing to HK$2.375 in early morning trade. A total of 119.57 million shares changed hands. The company offered 100 million shares to the public.
